date: Nov 20, 2026 · Week 2 / Day 5 · Decision-driven meetings and tradeoffs

cards.title: A recommendation, not a menu
cards.question: PCIe Gen5 margin can gain 0.5 dB through a connector ECO, but it costs five days. What do you recommend at the release review?
cards.selfCheck: State your preferred path, system benefit, schedule cost and reversal trigger. Exercise: give a 30-second recommendation with one explicit ask.
cards.prompt: Role-play a release director. Challenge my PCIe ECO recommendation, including opportunity cost, evidence and a decision deadline.

cards.title: How much proof is enough?
cards.question: EM predicts a 52-ohm launch; TDR reads 55 ohms. Layout freeze is tomorrow. What minimum evidence changes your decision?
cards.selfCheck: Separate model uncertainty from actual channel risk. Exercise: specify one discriminating test, an acceptance threshold and the fallback if results arrive late.
cards.prompt: Act as lab and EM leads disputing launch impedance. Make me define decision-relevant proof, deadline and conditional action.

cards.title: Two fires, one lab slot
cards.question: A 20 MHz PDN peak and a PCIe eye-margin concern both need validation today. How do you allocate the only lab slot?
cards.selfCheck: Rank by release impact, uncertainty reduction and decision urgency—not who asks loudest. Exercise: defend a test order and communicate the deferred risk.
cards.prompt: Give me a lab-capacity conflict between PDN and PCIe. Challenge my prioritization and stakeholder update.

cards.title: Make the yes safe
cards.question: Layout resists a crosstalk reroute because it threatens the schedule. How do you win agreement without authority?
cards.selfCheck: Offer a bounded experiment, objective pass/fail criteria and a pre-agreed fallback. Exercise: make a 25-second ask that respects layout constraints.
cards.prompt: Role-play a skeptical layout manager. Coach me to secure a crosstalk mitigation decision without relying on authority.

cards.title: The decision board in 60 seconds
cards.question: At a design gate, PCIe, PDN and crosstalk risks compete. Can you lead the meeting to one defensible release decision?
cards.selfCheck: Use Week 1 risk-first visibility plus Week 2 decision rights: recommendation, top uncertainty, owners and checkpoint. Exercise: deliver a 60-second gate brief and a 15-second version.
cards.prompt: Simulate a cross-functional SI/PI release gate. Score my 60-second synthesis on risk clarity, tradeoffs, decision authority and follow-through.
